title: Cognizant dedicates more than 25000 professionals to Claude delivery
content:
- Cognizant's new Claude Frontier Capability Group brings more than 25,000 professionals together in a dedicated global Claude delivery organization.
- Cognizant's new managed services model gives clients one accountable partner for running Claude in production, with more predictable AI spend and enterprise-grade controls.
TEANECK, N.J., Nov. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Cognizant (Nasdaq: CTSH) today announced the formation of the Claude Frontier Capability Group, more than 25,000 professionals committed to delivering Claude for clients. The group is focused on execution excellence, transformation and client success, with the scale to take AI from pilot to production across enterprises' core operations.
Enterprises have access to frontier AI capability but continue to face challenges in delivering value to the business. Cognizant has built Claude skills throughout its workforce, with more than 44,000 associates in business units and corporate functions already trained or certified on Claude. The new group is a dedicated organization building and running Claude-powered systems inside client businesses.
Cognizant is also introducing a managed services model for Claude. Under the model, Cognizant manages the operation of Claude-powered systems in production on clients' behalf, so they can focus on the business results it makes possible. Both initiatives draw on Cognizant's Frontier workforce model, through which it is developing Frontier Certified Engineers and Frontier Business Operators credentialed directly by frontier-model companies.  
"Clients want a partner who will take responsibility for delivery once AI is running inside their business," said Ravi Kumar S, CEO of Cognizant. "We are putting more than 25,000 of our people on Claude and taking on the job of running it for clients through managed services. That is a significant bet on Claude, and on what enterprises can achieve with it in their core operations."
"Every enterprise is racing to bring AI into its organization, but the people with the skills to make it work inside a real business have become the hardest talent to find," said Paul Smith, Chief Commercial Officer, Anthropic. "Cognizant is working to address that gap, committing more than 25,000 people to help their customers put Claude to work across their businesses."
A managed services model for Claude
Cognizant's managed services model supports the operation of Claude in production for clients, combining dedicated talent, licensed access to Claude and Cognizant's own IP, including its AI Delivery Operating System. The model gives clients more predictable AI spend and runs every engagement within enterprise-grade security and governance controls, customized to each client's connectivity, architecture and risk requirements.

report.summary: Cognizant created a 25,000-person Claude delivery group and a managed service for running Claude in enterprise production.
report.background: Enterprises have rushed to test generative AI, but many pilots stall because they lack people who can integrate models into core workflows, manage security, and control costs. System integrators are now competing to become the accountable layer between frontier model providers and business operations. Anthropic has been expanding enterprise distribution through cloud partners and consultancies, while Cognizant has trained tens of thousands of staff on Claude and created frontier-model credentials. The Claude Frontier Capability Group turns that training into a dedicated delivery organization, and the managed-services model mirrors how enterprises already buy cloud and application operations: licensed technology plus human expertise, governance, and SLAs. It also signals that AI adoption is moving from experimentation to production operations, where predictability, risk controls, and vendor accountability matter as much as model quality.
key_points: Cognizant is grouping more than 25,000 employees into a dedicated Claude Frontier Capability Group. The unit is meant to build and run Claude-powered systems inside client businesses, moving beyond pilots into core operations. Cognizant says over 44,000 associates have already been trained or certified on Claude, giving it a large pool to draw from.

The new managed service makes Cognizant the accountable operator of Claude systems in production. It combines dedicated staff, licensed Claude access, and Cognizant IP such as its AI Delivery Operating System. Clients get more predictable AI spending and enterprise-grade security and governance controls customized to their architecture, connectivity, and risk needs.

Both initiatives rely on Cognizant's Frontier workforce model, which credentials engineers and business operators directly with frontier-model companies. That is an attempt to solve the AI skills gap by creating recognizable, vendor-aligned roles rather than generic AI training. For clients, it offers a signal that delivery staff have validated Claude skills; for Cognizant, it differentiates its services from general IT consulting.

CEO Ravi Kumar S frames the move as a significant bet on Claude and on enterprise AI in core operations. Anthropic's Paul Smith highlights the shortage of people who can make AI work inside real businesses. The partnership gives Anthropic a large services channel and gives Cognizant a frontier-model anchor for repeatable enterprise offers.
report.impact: For the AI industry, this validates a services-led adoption path: model vendors supply capability, while integrators supply talent, governance, and production operations. It could push competitors to announce similar dedicated practices and make managed AI operations a standard enterprise purchase. Developers may see more Claude-centric enterprise projects, credential requirements, and demand for skills in agent orchestration, evaluation, security, and cost controls. It also raises lock-in concerns: clients may standardize on Claude plus one integrator. Regular users are likely to encounter Claude-powered workflows in customer service, back-office, and internal tools, with more human oversight and compliance guardrails, but also less visible choice about which model powers those systems.
report.tools: To follow this trend, watch Anthropic's Claude Enterprise and API, Claude Code for developer workflows, and the Model Context Protocol (MCP) for connecting Claude to enterprise systems. For hands-on prototyping, open-source LangGraph or CrewAI can model multi-agent orchestration, while LangSmith or Arize Phoenix can help with evaluation and observability. Cognizant's AI Delivery Operating System is proprietary, so readers should compare its managed-service claims with public cloud AI operations offerings.
